h: Keep Your Cool, Keep Your Line
p: Liverpool loves a bit of competition, and it's easy to let that spill over on track. But the drivers who win are usually the ones who stay calm. Racing hard is great; racing angry is slow.

A few basics will make a big difference. Brake in a straight line before you turn, rather than in the middle of the bend. Look ahead to the exit of each corner, not at the kart in front, and use the whole width of the track. Go in wide, cut to the inside, and let the kart run wide again on the way out.
When it comes to overtaking, be patient. A clean pass on the inside of a corner is worth ten wild lunges that end in the barrier, and staff will take a dim view of anyone driving dangerously.

Leave yourself time to get there. Lime Street station puts you right in the city centre, with regular trains from Manchester, Chester and across Merseyside, so getting your group together for race day is pretty painless.

Liverpool has plenty to keep you busy after the race. Fans can tour Anfield, home of Liverpool FC, or wander through Sefton Park with its Victorian Palm House. The World Museum on William Brown Street has a planetarium and an aquarium alongside its natural history collections. The city's Georgian Quarter is lovely for a stroll too.
